 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers vs Tulsa Golden Hurricane Prediction, 11/16/2026 College Basketball Picks, Best Bets & Odds
 by Guy Bruhn - 11/15/2026 
 Game: Western Kentucky Hilltoppers vs Tulsa Golden Hurricane
 Date: Monday, November 16, 2026
 Location: Reynolds Center in Tulsa, OK
 TV: ESPN+
 The Western Kentucky Hilltoppers (3-1) are headed to Reynolds Center on Monday where they will meet the Tulsa Golden Hurricane (3-0).
 The Western Kentucky Hilltoppers stepped onto the hardwood against Campbellsville and took home the win by a score of 78-51 in their last contest. Western Kentucky finished the game having earned a 44.1% field goal percentage (30 out of 68) and converted 6 out of their 23 shots from downtown. From the free throw line, the Hilltoppers made 12 of 16 tries for a rate of 75.0%. When it comes to pulling down boards, they compiled 36 with 12 of them being offensive. They also recorded 16 assists for this contest in addition to forcing the opposition into 24 turnovers and getting 17 steals. In relation to the defense, Western Kentucky allowed the other team to shoot 38.0% from the field on 19 out of 50 shooting. Campbellsville recorded 14 assists and had 4 steals for the game. Additionally, Campbellsville grabbed 27 rebounds (4 offensive, 23 defensive), but wasn't able to record a rejection. Campbellsville finished the game shooting 33.3% from the free throw line by knocking down 2 of 6 attempts. They also converted 11 out of their 26 shots from 3-point land. Regarding fouls, the Hilltoppers finished with 7 while Campbellsville racked up 12 fouls.
 Emondrek Erkins-Ford is one guy who was a factor for this contest. He ended up finishing with 14 points on 6 out of 10 shooting. He was on the court for 22 minutes played and snagged 4 rebounds. He ended up going 60.0% from the field but finished the game without an assist.

 Western Kentucky will take the court with a win-loss mark of 3-1 on the year. They cough up possession 9.8 times per contest and as a team they commit 13.8 personal fouls every game. As a unit, Western Kentucky is grabbing 42.5 boards per contest and has earned 63 assists for the campaign, which is 95th in the country in terms of passing the ball. The Hilltoppers are hitting 32.1% on shots from downtown (27 of 84) and 75.6% from the free throw line. They average 84.3 points per outing (120th in college) while hitting 44.0% from the field.
 Defensively, the Hilltoppers are able to force 18.5 turnovers per game while drawing 15.5 fouls. They are relinquishing 38.3% on shots from downtown and they are ranked 71st in the nation in opponents points per game (63.5). The Hilltoppers defense is allowing a FG percentage of 38.0% (82 of 216) and they surrender 34.0 rebounds per game as a team. They rank 301st in college in allowing assists to their opponents with 60 relinquished for the campaign.
 The last time they took the hardwood, the Tulsa Golden Hurricane walked away with a victory by a final of 80-71 against Oral Roberts. The Golden Hurricane were able to pull down 25 defensive rebounds and 16 offensive rebounds for a total of 41 for this game. They also coughed it up 16 times, while getting 8 steals for this contest. Oral Roberts was called for 23 fouls in this contest which took the Golden Hurricane to the free throw line for a total of 28 tries. They were able to knock down 23 of the free throws for a rate of 82.1%. Regarding three-point attempts, Tulsa made 7 out of their 28 tries (25.0%). When all was said and done, the Golden Hurricane ended up going 25 out of 55 from the field which gave them a percentage of 45.5%. The Golden Hurricane allowed Oral Roberts to knock down 23 out of 64 tries from the floor which left them with a shooting percentage of 35.9% in the game. They finished 31.3% from downtown by connecting on 10 of 32 and finished the game at 15 out of 22 at the free throw line (68.2%). In relation to cleaning up the glass, Tulsa allowed Oral Roberts to grab 28 overall (16 offensive).
 Denton Forsythe was important for the Golden Hurricane for the game. He accumulated 18 points in his 22 mins on the hardwood and earned 5 assists in this game. He knocked down 4 of 6 for this game giving him a field goal percentage of 66.7%, and had 6 rebounds.
 Tulsa has a record of 3-0 this season. As an offensive unit, the Golden Hurricane are hitting on 48.3% from the field, which is ranked 102nd in Division 1. Tulsa has totaled 272 pts so far this season (90.7 per game) and they average 43.0 rebounds per contest. They are earning an assist 16.0 times per game (147th in the nation) and they turn it over 12.3 times per game. The Golden Hurricane are responsible for committing 16.0 fouls per game and they go 72.1% from the free throw line.
 The Tulsa defense gives up 34.5% on 3-point attempts (30 of 87) and opponents are connecting on 75.0% of their foul shots. They surrender 11.3 assists and 26.7 total rebounds per game, which has them ranked 108th and 9th in the country. The Golden Hurricane defensively are ranked 90th in D-1 in PPG surrendered with 65.3. They are able to force 13.0 TO's per game and have allowed teams to shoot 38.5% from the field (86th in Division 1).
 Who will win tonight's NCAA game against the spread?
 Guy Bruhn's Pick: Take Western Kentucky
